messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify buffer_trim removes both leading and trailing whitespace from a buffer containing spaces at both ends.
test_metadata.rationale: This test ensures the function correctly trims whitespace from both sides, exercising both buffer_trim_left and buffer_trim_right, and validates in-place modification and length update.

path_conditions: self is a valid, non-NULL buffer_t*
buffer contains both leading and trailing whitespace

assertions.name: helper_assert_buffer_content
assertions.purpose: Verify buffer's content matches expected trimmed string
assertions.usage: After buffer_trim, check buffer->data is as expected

assertions.name: helper_assert_buffer_length
assertions.purpose: Verify buffer's string length matches expected value
assertions.usage: After buffer_trim, check buffer_length(buffer) is correct

utilities.name: helper_create_buffer_with_content
utilities.purpose: Create a buffer initialized with a given string
utilities.usage: Setup: create buffer with leading and trailing whitespace

utilities.name: helper_cleanup_buffer
utilities.purpose: Free the memory allocated for a buffer

preconditions: Buffer contains both leading and trailing whitespace
setup_requirements.initial_state:
A buffer containing the string "   hello world	 
" (spaces before and after, tab and newline at end)

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Buffer with leading and trailing whitespace
primary_function_args.concrete_value: buffer created with content "   hello world\t \n"
primary_function_args.rationale: Triggers both buffer_trim_left and buffer_trim_right to remove whitespace from both ends

return_value.description: No return value; buffer is modified in place

side_effects.effect: Buffer's content is trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace
Buffer's string length is updated to match trimmed content

invariants_maintained: No memory leaks or buffer overflows

assertions_required.description: Buffer content matches expected trimmed string
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Trimming did not remove all leading/trailing whitespace

assertions_required.description: Buffer length matches length of trimmed string
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Buffer length not updated correctly after trimming

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All memory freed, no resource leaks

operation_sequence: Create buffer with content "   hello world\t \n" using helper_create_buffer_with_content
Assert buffer->data equals "hello world" using helper_assert_buffer_content
edge_cases_to_note: Buffer with only whitespace (not tested here)
Buffer with no whitespace (not tested here)

path_coverage_analysis.description: Standard path: buffer_trim_left and buffer_trim_right called on valid buffer

integration_test_suggestions: Test buffer_trim on buffer with only whitespace
Test buffer_trim on buffer with no whitespace
Test buffer_trim on buffer with internal (not leading/trailing) whitespace
